Mia L.: Heads up — seeing an 8-12% tail latency regression on the AWQ int8 weight-only path after yesterday's packing refactor. Captured a flame and a KV hit histogram.

perf-bot: nightly-perf-run #1865: int8-weightonly-serving: median +0.5%, p99 +11.2% vs baseline. See attached run id 2026-03-17T23:40Z. :chart_with_upwards_trend:

Raj P.: Can you paste the flame and the KV cache hit rates? wondering if this is pure packing overhead or a cache miss pattern.

Mia L.: flame (truncated):
```
flame: pack_unload 42%
flame: kv_lookup 9%
flame: int8_grouped_spmm_v2 18%
flame: fallback_gemm 7%
flame: aten::conv 6%
```
KV cache stats (sampled 5k requests):
```
kv_hits: 62%
kv_misses: 38%
avg_prefix_len: 12
seq_len_dist: 8-64 (median 28)
```
Looks like pack_unload is dominating.

Olga K.: Hmm, pack_unload blowing up suggests packing/unpacking is happening more frequently or at wrong granularity. Did the refactor change group_size or the boundary check for reuse? @Mia L. did you keep group_size the same (32)? :eyes:

Mia L.: group_size remained 32. The patch moved packing earlier (pre-batch) to try to amortize work... but profiler shows it's running per-request in many cases. Might be a routing bug that invalidates packed buffers when batcher splits requests.

Dan S.: Seeing something similar on matmul routing: if request alignment != pack_alignment we fallback to the generic kernel which also forces an unpack. Logs show: 
```
[runtime] picked kernel: int8_grouped_spmm_v2 (alignment ok)
[runtime] picked kernel: int8_gemm_fallback (alignment mismatch)
[pack] cache invalidated: batcher_split=true route=dedupe
```
If pack buffers get invalidated by the batcher split, we pay pack/unpack repeatedly.

Raj P.: Could be interaction between continuous batching heuristics and pack dedupe. The batcher will split to honor hard latency SLOs which can produce small micro-batches and trigger pack recompute. Can you run an A/B where pack dedupe is disabled so it always reuses the buffer vs current behavior? Also try group_size=64 for AWQ to reduce packing frequency.

Mia L.: Ran quick microbench (seq=32, model=redwood-awq-7b, batch sizes 1..8):
```
config A (group=32, pack-dedupe=on): batch=1 median=28.6ms p99=85.2ms pack_unload=46%
config B (group=64, pack-dedupe=on): batch=1 median=29.4ms p99=78.1ms pack_unload=38%
config C (group=32, pack-dedupe=off): batch=1 median=27.9ms p99=74.6ms pack_unload=25%
```
So disabling dedupe reduced pack cost (weirdly) — seems reuse semantics might be busted: dedupe path invalidates previously packed layout.

Olga K.: That matches my hypothesis. If dedupe tries to canonicalize key shapes it might evict and re-pack. For AWQ/group-weight-only, larger group_size reduces number of pack ops but increases per-op work. We need a follow-up: ensure pack dedupe marks buffers as reusable across batch splits and update the batcher to pass canonical shape.

Dan S.: I pushed a small prototype that tags packed buffers with a stable canonical id and prevents eviction on split. snippet: 
```
--- a/runtime/pack_cache.cpp
+++ b/runtime/pack_cache.cpp
@@
- if (batcher_split) evict(packed_id);
+ if (batcher_split && !packed_meta.canonical) evict(packed_id);
```
No functional changes yet — just a guard. Will run internal perf tests.

perf-bot: pre-merge micro-run #1865-proto: median -0.4%, p99 -5.8% vs current main for int8-weightonly path. KV hit steady.

Raj P.: Nice. Also can we add a unit test that simulates batcher splits and asserts the pack cache keeps canonical buffers? Catches regressions.

Mia L.: Added test + local run looks good. Also validated that group_size=64 + canonical pack yields slightly higher median but better tail; might be acceptable tradeoff for webapps where p99 matters more.

Olga K.: Agree. Next steps: 1) land canonical buffer guard, 2) add unit/regression test, 3) try smarter batching hint that prefers coalescing requests with same canonical shape, 4) run 24h e2e perf.

Mia L.: I'm going to open a PR with the guard + test. Will roll to canary after CI. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

Dan S.: I'll add a small metric (pack_reuse_ratio) to the console so we can alert if reuse drops.

perf-bot: scheduled perf-run e2e #1866 in 2 hours.

Mia L.: Updated — PR at https://git.local/redwood/runtime/pull/2145, includes logs and perf snapshots. Follow-up after canary.
